title: Tesla’s Cybercab fleet jumped 8x in a month, with Dallas up next
source_used: Teslarati (read in full from the pre-fetched text; the page also carries unrelated Musk/Starlink stories, which were ignored)
key_facts: Tesla's Robotaxi account on X said on 10 Oct 2026 that the service had 'scaled to 300+ Cybercabs serving Austin', an 8x increase in 30 days.
It is the first time Tesla has put an official number on its active Cybercab fleet.
Ashok Elluswamy, Tesla's head of AI software, wrote 'Dallas soon'; it is the first time Tesla has named the next city for public Cybercab rides.
Public Cybercab rides opened in Austin on 4 Sep 2026, a day after an invite-only launch event.
Texas records show 319 registered Cybercabs, up from 169 after 150 were added on Thursday (8 Oct); the first seven appeared on 31 Aug.

RobotaxiTracker, a community site counting from sightings and state records, listed 275 vehicles in unsupervised service in Austin on Saturday, 105 of them Cybercabs, well below Tesla's figure; its counts can lag.
NHTSA opened an audit query into Tesla's certification that the Cybercab meets federal safety standards; sworn answers are due 30 Oct. Tesla reports third-quarter earnings on 21 Oct.
quote_evidence: Tesla says more than 300 Cybercabs are now serving Austin, the first time the company has put an official number on its active Cybercab fleet.
On Thursday, Tesla added 150 Cybercabs to the Texas automated vehicle registry, lifting its registered count to 319 from 169.
NHTSA opened an audit query into Tesla’s certification that the Cybercab meets federal safety standards, and sworn answers are due October 30.
why_it_matters_hint: Tesla's driverless taxi service in Austin is growing fast by Tesla's own count and a second city is hinted, while a federal safety review is open.
notes: The 300+ figure is Tesla's own. The community tracker's 105 Cybercabs in service is lower, and the article says tracker counts can lag. Teslarati is a Tesla-focused outlet.
